business_problem: Researchers at the Austrian Academy of Sciences needed a way to analyze and reconstruct huge volumes of fragmented Ancient Greek texts that manual transcription and interpretation could not process quickly or at sufficient scale.
solution_summary: The Austrian Academy of Sciences is building Apollo, a custom large language model for Ancient Greek, to turn large-scale classical text analysis into an interactive AI workflow. The project combines a 600 million-word historical Greek corpus with tens of thousands of published inscriptions and papyri so the model can learn the linguistic variation needed to reconstruct missing passages and surface thematic links across collections. Mistral contributed model-building expertise and, with services partner Reply, helped establish a secure European-based infrastructure for training and use. Researchers can now apply Apollo to damaged texts that previously required years of manual transcription and interpretation, and the platform is being extended toward semantic search and handwritten inscription decipherment so scholars can move from recovery of fragments to broader historical analysis.

solution_components.name: Apollo
solution_components.role: Acts as the custom Ancient Greek language model used to restore text and support scholarly discovery.

data_flow: Historical Greek texts, published inscriptions, and papyri feed Apollo's training corpus; researchers submit fragmentary or damaged text to the model, Apollo proposes restorations and semantic matches, and the outputs let scholars move into interpretation and broader historical analysis faster.
business_outcome: Apollo lets researchers reconstruct damaged Ancient Greek texts in hours instead of years, opens a path to working through more than one million unread papyri, and creates a foundation for semantic search and future handwritten inscription decipherment.
